warning_texts: This profile is deliberately single-vendor: the architect, four workers, five auditors and this red team are all claude-opus-5, an isolated context is not an independent vendor, no GPT or other cross-vendor gate exists anywhere in this system, and the only controls that hold independently are the de

Writes over raw_data and the frozen machinery were closed only by permissions.deny for the edit tools, not for the shell, so a changed raw file would be caught after the fact by the control lock rather than prevented; this red team saw no sign of tampering but did not verify raw digests against the

All five auditor results (gate0_semantic, gate_clean_auditor, gate_metrics_auditor, gate_claims_auditor, gate_release_auditor) have summaries of the form 'driver e2e <step>', evidence notes that say only 'driver e2e evidence' and a placeholder created_at of 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, and the metrics and
gate_release_auditor passed the release on a single refund-rate comparison and did not read the report's prose, which is how the population-line contradiction reached the final gate.

All four worker results (worker_clean, worker_metrics, worker_analysis, worker_release) are 'driver e2e' stubs with empty warnings, no disclosures field and a placeholder created_at, so the absence of disclosed deviations says nothing about what the workers actually ran.

Report prose (title, population line, the closing reconciliation sentence) is covered by no deterministic rule: caveats_rendered proves only that each claim's caveats are present, and release_surface_contract.json has empty card_caveat_requirements and visual_evidence, so any statement on the page o

gate_release_document's only two rules, claims_rendered and caveats_rendered, sit under accepted_unproven in check_plan.json because the plan proof crashed with FileNotFoundError, so neither rule has ever been shown to fire on a broken release and their PASS here is unproven.

The spec period ends 2025-03-30, while R01 asks about the reported quarter, the exclusion reason says outside the reported quarter, the metrics period is named 2025-Q1-delivered and the spec comment treats a 2025-04-01 order as the boundary test, which together suggest the intended end is 2025-03-31

The refund_rate_basis ruling fixes the unit (paying customers) but not what makes a customer refunded: the release counts any customer with a refund above zero, partial refunds included (27/57 = 0.473684), while counting only fully refunded customers gives 12/57 = 0.210526, so the headline refund ra

On the order-row basis the refund rate would be 33/174 = 0.189655, 2.498 times smaller than the customer basis, which matches the risk register's roughly 2.5x and not the spec comment's roughly a factor of three.

Revenue recognition net_of_refunds deducts each refund against the original order's order_date because the export carries no refund date, so any refund issued after 2025-03-30 for a first-quarter order is inside the 4,493.50 EUR deducted from net revenue 35,741.52 and the country figures; whether th
order_date is a bare date with no time component, so the Europe/Warsaw timezone ruling cannot be tested on this export and moves no number here.

All four worker carries define the population as status=delivered and leave the period out of that field (only the name and the periods block carry it), so a stage that read only the definition would lose the period boundary.

All four worker carries list raw_data/orders.csv under do_not_reread, but that is a raw source, not an output of a previous stage as common contract rule 26 intends; it is harmless here because every downstream number reproduces.

The release does not tell its reader that R05 (customer lifetime value) was declined for lack of acquisition dates, or that 27 raw rows were excluded (26 not delivered, 1 delivered row dated 2025-04-01, O00201); both facts live only in analysis/answers and check_plan.json.

The no-literal rule for the release generator src/release/build_release.py rests on the machine release gate alone, and the release_surface_gate.json evidence lists rendered numbers but records no generator-literal scan result, so this red team cannot confirm that scan ran.
excluded_outside_period has no direct machine recompute and is pinned only by the row-accounting sum; this red team recomputed it independently as 1 (O00201).
The dashboard has no top-level population statement, only the period, so the delivered-only population reaches a dashboard reader only through each card's caveats.

Not established by this red team: the carries' conformance to audit/schemas/carry.schema.json, the generator source, the contents of gate_metrics_machine/evidence/unchecked.json, and retry history or stale inputs, which a human should read with audit_runner.py report; the handoff has no drift_since_
summary: Every published figure reproduces exactly from raw_data/orders.csv with this stage's own code (net revenue 35741.52 EUR, PL 11181.67, DE 11032.61, CZ 13527.24, refund rate 27/57 = 0.473684, row accounting 201 = 174 + 26 + 1), clean_data equals the spec population row for row, and all 21 rendered numbers on the three release surfaces match. The release still fails on one material blocker: release/report.md line 3 tells the reader the population is all orders inside the period, which contradicts the spec population (delivered only), the report's own title and every card caveat.
